messages.content:
You are checking a research plan against a list of experimental controls. You are not asked whether the plan is good. For each control of the list you give two separate answers: CONTENT (does the plan state this control?) and PLACE (is the passage written under an experiment that it can check?).

PLAN. A sequence of actions written one after the other by a planner. Each action adds or revises one proposed experiment and usually has the fields ACTION, TITLE, PROPOSAL, CONTROLS, COST and PREDICTION. Actions are separated by blank lines and are given in the order they were written. Every action counts, including an action that revises an earlier one and an action that looks incomplete.

REFERENCE CONTROLS. A list of experimental controls. Each has an identifier and a description.

CONTENT. Give exactly one content status for each reference control. Judge the content only, wherever the passage is written in the plan.
- "conforme": a passage of the plan states what the description requires (what is compared, held fixed, varied, repeated, measured or excluded). Different wording is fine. Nothing essential is missing or weakened.
- "altere": a passage of the plan states a recognisable but partial, vaguer, reduced or modified version of the control.
- "absent": no passage of the plan states this control.
If the control is stated in several places, keep the best content status found (conforme, then altere, then absent) and quote the passage that earns it. If several passages earn the same best status, quote one whose PLACE is "checks" if there is one.

PLACE. Only for "conforme" and "altere". Read the action that contains your quote, and judge it against the experiment that this action proposes (its TITLE and PROPOSAL), not against the description of the reference control. If that action has no TITLE and no PROPOSAL, answer "general" if the quoted control is general, otherwise "cannot_check".
- "checks": this experiment is one whose result the quoted control would check.
- "cannot_check": this experiment has nothing for the quoted control to compare, hold fixed, vary, repeat, measure or exclude.
- "general": the quoted control names no model, dataset, metric, quantity, condition or comparison that belongs to one experiment; it would apply to any experiment of the plan.
For "absent", PLACE is null. Your PLACE answer must never change your CONTENT answer.

Rules.
1. Judge each reference control on its own. One passage may support several controls.
2. Judge only what is written. Do not credit a control because it would be sensible, usual or implied. Do not lower a status for style, length, order or cost.
3. Evidence. For "conforme" and "altere", quote the passage that carries the control. Copy it character for character from a single action: no ellipsis, no added or removed word, no corrected spelling, no changed punctuation, no paraphrase. Take the shortest passage that is enough: at least 24 characters, at most 300 characters; if the whole field that carries the control is shorter than 24 characters, quote the whole field. A program searches the plan for your quote, word for word; a quote that is not found counts as "absent".
4. For "absent", the quote is null.
5. Give an answer for every reference control, and for no other identifier.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else, in this form:
{"<identifier>": {"content": "conforme" | "altere" | "absent", "quote": "<quote>" | null, "place": "checks" | "cannot_check" | "general" | null}, ...}

PLAN
<<<
ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of removing the warm-up phase on rank correlation with the gold ordering for Varnok-2B
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Varnok-2B on the Avenel retrieval pool and measure rank correlation with the gold ordering before and after removing the warm-up phase.
CONTROLS: (1) Match the number of training steps between Varnok-2B and Corvane-12.
COST: 18 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Rank correlation with the gold ordering degrades on the Wexcombe caption set while it holds on the Avenel retrieval pool.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of masking named entities on area under the detection curve for Marrow-3
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Marrow-3 on the Brenna-QA set and measure area under the detection curve before and after masking named entities.
CONTROLS: (1) Repeat the evaluation of area under the detection curve on the Brenna-QA set with a second prompt template.
COST: 7 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Area under the detection curve improves by a small but reliable margin on the Brenna-QA set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of truncating the context to 2,000 tokens on pass rate on hidden tests for Quillon-L
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Quillon-L on the Osric code suite and measure pass rate on hidden tests before and after truncating the context to 2,000 tokens.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on the Tolwyn dialogue logs as a held-out distribution.
COST: 9 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Pass rate on hidden tests improves by a small but reliable margin on the Osric code suite.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of adding label noise at 10% on agreement with the reference labels for Halden-S
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Halden-S on the Lowick tabular benchmark and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after adding label noise at 10%.
CONTROLS: (1) Ablate adding label noise at 10% alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on agreement with the reference labels.
COST: 28 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in agreement with the reference labels beyond seed noise on the Lowick tabular benchmark.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of freezing the first twelve layers on exact-match accuracy for Dromond-8
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Dromond-8 on the Marisol summaries and measure exact-match accuracy before and after freezing the first twelve layers.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on the Halvard corpus as a held-out distribution.
COST: 33 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: No change in exact-match accuracy beyond seed noise on the Marisol summaries.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of removing the warm-up phase on rank correlation with the gold ordering for Varnok-2B
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Varnok-2B on the Avenel retrieval pool and measure rank correlation with the gold ordering before and after removing the warm-up phase.
CONTROLS: (1) Ablate removing the warm-up phase alone, keeping data and optimizer fixed, to isolate its effect on rank correlation with the gold ordering.
COST: 6 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Rank correlation with the gold ordering degrades on the Wexcombe caption set while it holds on the Avenel retrieval pool.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of masking named entities on area under the detection curve for Marrow-3
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Marrow-3 on the Brenna-QA set and measure area under the detection curve before and after masking named entities.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on the Kettering proofs as a held-out distribution.
COST: 15 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Area under the detection curve improves by a small but reliable margin on the Brenna-QA set.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of truncating the context to 2,000 tokens on pass rate on hidden tests for Quillon-L
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Quillon-L on the Osric code suite and measure pass rate on hidden tests before and after truncating the context to 2,000 tokens.
CONTROLS: (1) Report calibration error on the Osric code suite to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric.
COST: 9 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Pass rate on hidden tests improves by a small but reliable margin on the Osric code suite.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of adding label noise at 10% on agreement with the reference labels for Halden-S
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Halden-S on the Lowick tabular benchmark and measure agreement with the reference labels before and after adding label noise at 10%.
CONTROLS: (1) Evaluate on the Pryce reasoning chains as a held-out distribution.
COST: 32 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Agreement with the reference labels improves by a small but reliable margin on the Lowick tabular benchmark.

ACTION: add
TITLE: Effect of freezing the first twelve layers on exact-match accuracy for Dromond-8
PROPOSAL: We fine-tune Dromond-8 on the Marisol summaries and measure exact-match accuracy before and after freezing the first twelve layers.
CONTROLS: (1) Report false-alarm rate at fixed recall on the Marisol summaries to check that the gain is not an artifact of one metric.
COST: 9 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Exact-match accuracy improves by a small but reliable margin on the Marisol summaries.
>>>

REFERENCE CONTROLS
- id: c1 | description: Evaluate on the Halvard corpus, a distribution that was not used for training.
- id: c2 | description: Isolate the effect of removing the warm-up phase on rank correlation with the gold ordering by changing it alone, with data and optimizer held fixed.
- id: c3 | description: Compare against Tessel-9 as a baseline trained with an identical budget.
